page: Google Cloud Platform m4-megamem-112 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for exceptionally memory-dense workloads. It provides 112 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1488.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 13.29 GB per virtual processor. The instance contains zero hardware accelerators and does not include bundled local storage disks.

Architecturally, the dedicated CPU allocation guarantees consistent compute access without multi-tenant vCPU contention. The lack of integrated local disks requires deployment architectures to rely on remote block storage solutions for persistent data management. Furthermore, the configuration provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external networking allocation or private network routing for inbound connectivity.

Given the expansive memory footprint per core, m4-megamem-112 targets enterprise-scale in-memory databases, large caching layers, and memory-bound transactional applications. In terms of resource efficiency, the instance allows consolidation of extensive datasets within a single virtual machine boundary, avoiding the networking overhead of distributed cache nodes while trading off integrated disk storage for external storage provisioning.

The dedicated vCPU provisioning ensures stable processing capacity free from resource contention across multi-tenant environments. Without complimentary public IPv4 networking out of the box, infrastructure architects must configure external IP routing appropriately. Due to its exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio, this configuration targets memory-intensive enterprise workloads, in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, and large data analytics pipelines requiring massive unpartitioned system RAM.
